reading.body:
Chris Stewart is named on 5 AI lobbying filings, all filed through one firm, for a single client, and those filings name 15 separate bills.

The pattern is narrow and deep. One lobbyist, one firm, one client, and a long list of legislation. Breadth across 15 bills is the notable figure here, not the count of filings. A single client retaining a single firm to touch that many AI-related bills describes a concentrated advocacy operation rather than a scattered one.

The prior government position matters for AI specifically because it is the mechanism by which legislative access is bought and disclosed. The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires filers to list covered positions held in the prior twenty years, and this record shows a former US Congressman serving 2013 to 2023. That is the revolving door stated as a filing requirement, not as an allegation.

What this does not tell the reader: whether any bill moved, what was said, what the client wanted, or what any of it cost. The data covers disclosure, not influence. It also does not connect to compute, buildings, or power, and nothing here should be read as doing so.
